metadata.title: Bookmark Scout – Save bookmarks to the right folder, fast
metadata.description: Browser extension that saves pages to the right bookmark folder: type a folder name, press a shortcut, or let AI suggest one. Plus search and cleanup.

features: Save to a folder by typing its name
Quick save shortcut with an in-page notification and undo
Side panel support (the sidebar in Firefox)
Undo and redo in the bookmarks manager
Bookmarks manager that works like Chrome's
Dead link scanning with reviewed repairs
Privacy review with optional redaction before exports
Opt-in AI chat that changes bookmarks only after you approve

languageSuggestion.label: Language suggestion
languageSuggestion.text: This page is also available in English.

footer.tagline: Save pages to the right folder, then find and tidy them, right in your browser.
footer.madeBy: Made by {author}, an independent developer: no company, no ads, no account. Free and open source.

hero.title: Save every page to the right folder, in seconds.
hero.description: Type part of a folder's name, or press {{SHORTCUT:commands.quick-save}} on any page, and the page is saved to the folder it belongs in. If you like, AI can suggest the folder too. Bookmark Scout also finds and tidies the bookmarks you already have, right in your browser. No account, no ads, and we don't track what you do.
hero.demoNote: This demo uses a made-up folder tree and keeps nothing. The extension shows your own folders, inside your browser.

demo.label: Try it: save this page to a folder
demo.placeholder: Type part of a folder name
demo.startHint: Type a few letters of a folder name. Matching folders appear here, nested ones included.
demo.alreadySaved: Already in {folder}, so it was not saved twice.
demo.emptyHint: Try part of a folder name, or a path such as ai/llms. A word of 4 letters or more may have one typo.

tour.title: What you can do with it
tour.lede: Real screenshots from the Chrome version. They follow your system's light or dark setting.
tour.firefoxNote: Firefox cannot replace its bookmarks page, so in Firefox the manager, with its cleanup tools, saved searches, and import and export, opens from a button in the toolbar popup.

save.heading: Save to the right folder
save.caption: The toolbar popup: type part of a folder's name, or pick a folder in the tree, and save the page in one click.
save.alt: Two popups: "fin" typed in the search box with the Fine-tuning folder (AI / LLMs) selected under Save to folder, and AI suggestions for another page: a new AI/LLMs/Inference folder and the existing AI/LLMs folder
points: Type part of a folder's name, even one nested deep in the tree, and save the current page there without leaving the keyboard
Type a path such as ai/llms, and still find the folder with a small typo
Press {{SHORTCUT:commands.quick-save}} on any page to save it to the folder that matches it best; a small notification in the page offers Undo and other folders
A page already in that folder is not saved twice, and folders you saved to recently come first
Save links from the right-click menu into recent folders, once you turn the menu on in Settings (it is off at first)
With AI turned on, get folder suggestions for the page, or save to the first one with {{SHORTCUT:commands.ai-quick-save}}

organize.heading: Find and organize what you saved
organize.caption: The manager replaces Chrome's Bookmarks page and works like it, with a folder tree, breadcrumbs, and a sortable table.
organize.alt: The Bookmark Scout manager on the AI / LLMs / Fine-tuning folder, with the folder tree (AI, Dev, Design, Tools, Reading list), one search box, and the bookmark table, each bookmark with its site's icon
points: Search all your bookmarks as you type, by title, address, folder, or tag
Keep the same tree and search open in the browser's side panel (the sidebar in Firefox)
Save a search, and it always shows the current results
Select several rows with {{SHORTCUT:mouse.select_toggle}}, right-click for cut, copy, paste, and open all, and drag bookmarks and folders where they belong
Undo and redo changes with {{SHORTCUT:manager.undo}} and {{SHORTCUT:manager.redo}}, even after a reload
Import bookmarks from a file after a preview, and export them as HTML, JSON, Markdown, or CSV
Link to a folder or a search, and move through it all with the keyboard

cleanUp.heading: Tidy years of saved links
cleanUp.caption: Duplicate Cleaner shows each group and the copy it keeps before anything is removed.
cleanUp.alt: The Duplicate Cleaner dialog listing two groups of duplicate bookmarks, each with the copy to keep marked, above a Remove duplicates button
points: Review duplicate groups, then remove the extra copies
Remove tracking codes from web addresses after a preview
Find dead links and repair them: delete, use the redirect, point to an archived copy, or edit the URL
Fetch page titles and apply only the ones you pick
Download each site's own icon, so bookmarks show it even in Firefox
Undo deletions and cleanups from the message that follows
See every change to your bookmarks in the History, even ones made outside Bookmark Scout, and get deleted ones back, even after the browser restarts

ai.heading: Optional AI, from the company you choose
ai.caption: AI is off until you turn it on. It needs an account with an AI company, which may charge a little each time you use it, or a free AI program on your own computer. In Chrome, its built-in AI suggests folders for free.
ai.alt: The AI tab in Settings: AI Features is on, and under Add service are two AI services the user added: a cloud AI company with its key hidden, set as the default, and a model on the computer
points: Get folder suggestions for the page you are on, or save to the first one with {{SHORTCUT:commands.ai-quick-save}}
Ask AI about your bookmarks: it searches them, checks links, and proposes moves, renames, and new folders as a plan that changes nothing until you approve it
Tag suggestions and short summaries that you review before saving
Folder reorganization plans, previewed before anything moves, with undo

noServer.title: No account, no server
noServer.body: There is nothing to sign up for, and Bookmark Scout has no server of its own. Your bookmarks are read and changed inside your browser.

noTelemetry.title: We don't track what you do
noTelemetry.body: The extension sends nothing to the developer: no analytics, no ads, no tracking.

aiOptIn.title: AI is off until you turn it on
aiOptIn.body: Then requests go straight from your browser to the AI company you chose, or stay on your computer with a free local AI program. AI programs on your computer get nothing until you allow them, and their changes wait for your approval.

exports.title: Exports get a privacy review
exports.body: Before a file downloads, a review flags private details, such as email addresses and login codes in links, and can hide them in the copy you save.

install.title: Add it to your browser
install.lede: It's free, and there is no account to create.
install.desktopOnly: Bookmark Scout works in a browser on a computer, not on phones or tablets.
install.permissions: {browser} asks for just one thing at install: “Read and change your bookmarks.” Other features ask only when you first use them. <docs>What it asks and why</docs>
install.advancedLede: Use this only to try Bookmark Scout in a browser whose store does not list it yet. You download it from GitHub, and a copy installed this way does not update on its own.

steps.download: Download bookmark-scout-*-chrome.zip from the latest release and extract it.
steps.open: Open chrome://extensions and turn on Developer mode in the top right.
steps.load: Click Load unpacked and select the extracted folder.

chrome.crx: The release also has a signed .crx file that you can drag onto the extensions page instead.

steps.download: Download bookmark-scout-*-edge.zip from the latest release and extract it.
steps.load: Click Load unpacked and select the extracted folder.

steps.download: Download bookmark-scout-*-firefox.zip from the latest release and extract it.
steps.load: Click Load Temporary Add-on and select manifest.json in the extracted folder.

firefox.limits: Firefox removes a temporary add-on when it restarts, so you load it again after each restart. In Firefox, the manager and its tools open from the Open bookmark manager button in the toolbar popup.

data.q: Does Bookmark Scout send my bookmarks anywhere?
data.a: No. Your bookmarks are read and changed inside your browser, and the extension sends nothing to the developer. Data leaves your browser only when you use an optional feature: AI requests go to the AI company you chose; checking links and fetching titles and site icons contact the bookmarked websites, after you allow it; and AI programs on your own computer that you connect (a feature for developers) get what they look up. Settings sync through your browser account if browser sync is on. The <privacy>privacy policy</privacy> has the details.

needAi.q: Do I need to use AI?
needAi.a: No. AI is optional. Saving, search, organizing, and cleanup all work without it, and AI stays off until you turn it on in Settings. To use AI, you need an account with an AI company, which may charge a little each time you use it, or a free AI program on your own computer.

providers.q: Which AI companies can I use?
providers.a: Bookmark Scout works with {providers}. Most AI companies need an account and a key from it, and charge a small amount for each use; Bookmark Scout itself charges nothing. Ollama runs AI on your own computer for free, if your computer is fast enough, and so does Chrome's built-in AI, which suggests folders. The <aiGuide>AI guide</aiGuide> shows how to set it up.

changes.q: Will it change my bookmarks without asking?
changes.a: No. Duplicate cleanup, URL cleanup, dead link repairs, fetched titles, AI reorganization, and imports all show a review before anything is written. AI features show their changes as a plan and wait for your approval. Deleting asks for confirmation by default, and the bookmarks manager can undo changes with {{SHORTCUT:manager.undo}}.

otherBrowsers.q: Does it work in Firefox and Edge?
otherBrowsers.a: Versions for Firefox and Edge are coming soon to their add-on stores. Until then, you can <install>install it by hand</install> from GitHub; Firefox removes a copy installed that way when it restarts. Firefox also cannot replace its bookmarks page, so there the manager opens from a button in the toolbar popup.

stores.q: Why is it not in the browser stores yet?
stores.a: Listings for the Chrome Web Store, Edge Add-ons, and Firefox Add-ons are being prepared, and each store reviews an extension before it goes live. Until then, install it from GitHub Releases.

free.a: Yes. Bookmark Scout is free and open source under {license}, with no ads and no paid plan. If you turn on AI, the AI company you use may charge for it.

who.a: An independent developer, not a company. There are no ads, no account, and nothing to buy, and anyone can read the source code on <source>GitHub</source>.

help.a: Start with the <support>support page</support> or the <docs>documentation</docs>. For help, email <email>{supportEmail}</email>. You can also report a problem in public on <github>GitHub</github>.
